chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who was found killed in a town, or between two towns. So he said: 'Measure what is between the two; whichever of the two is nearer, it is held responsible (for his blood/diyah).'
ai.seo_question: How is liability determined for a body found between two towns in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi outlines the principle of *qiyas* (geometric measurement) to assign liability for a found corpse (*murtaddah*) to the nearest settlement, reflecting the practical jurisprudence of the Imams in resolving ambiguous cases. It highlights the Shia legal emphasis on tangible evidence and proximity (*qurb*) when definitive proof of origin is lacking, ensuring fair distribution of *diyah* among potential responsible parties.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at Bin Mahran,

(The narrator) says, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the man who was found killed in the town, or in between two towns. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It would be compared what is between the two, so whichever of the two was nearer, would be responsible’.
